I'm putting a couple of questions to you, and if you don't understand some of these questions please ask me to rephrase them, and I will try to do so. You told us in your testimony that until October 1992 you were chef de cabinet for Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I fail to understand who was preceding -- who was succeeding you as the new chef de cabinet for Mr. Halilovic, could you please clarify that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: I can tell you that Sadika Omerhodzic aka Dika replaced me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm asking this because you mentioned a couple of times in your testimony also Sakib Mahmuljin could you clarify what the position of Mr. Mahmuljin was while Mr. Sadika Alihodzic [sic] was the chef de cabinet?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Sakib Mahmuljin was secretary of the Chief of Staff, Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that he was the deputy secretary? Can you just clarify please, the deputy secretary or the deputy chef de cabinet of Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No. These are two separate functions. Sefer had both the chef de cabinet and a secretary.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witnesses please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were asked to repeat your last sentence, please, witness.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: He had by establishment a head of office and a secretary. By establishment he also had a PR person who was Fahro Radoncic, an information officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Would it help you if I show you an order which might clear the situation? And I would ask that PT6289 be shown, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you will remember the situation when we objected to the tendering of documents through witnesses who were not on the list of the Prosecution evidence. This is one of the documents concerned. I would like my learned friend to clarify what this is about. What the purpose of the document is, whether to impeach the witness or to refresh his memory, in order for me to be able to react in relation to the document and possibly object, in keeping with our objection to such use of documents. Let me repeat: This document has not been on the list of the Prosecution evidence so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can just state that this document along with a couple of other documents has been communicated to my learned colleagues in advance of today's session. It is correct that this document was not on the Prosecution 65 ter list, but the witness summary which was communicated to us in advance of this witness appearing was referring to the fact that this witness was chef de cabinet and I believe the witness summary even said until summer 1993 and this document so to speak sheds some light who was on that information. We were departing from the information which was given to us in the witness summary and were selecting some documents which were properly communicated to my learned colleagues and a list with these new documents was also communicated to my learned colleagues before the examination-in-chief started today. As a final matter, I just want to say that in the course of the Prosecution's case several hundreds of documents were brought there by the Defence into evidence were admitted without the Prosecution having any prior notice about their existence, and in this case, as I have stated we have disclosed them before this testimony of the witness, and we have also communicated them on our list, exhibit list for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your learn friend wants you to explain the purpose for which you're tendering the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The purpose here is I was just dwelling on the position of Mr. Mahmuljin with the witness, and the answer I got is very close to the content of this document, and I'm sure that this witness can explain everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want to use the document to refresh the witness's memory to impeach the witness or do you want to refresh.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Not at all. It's not an impeachment document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's a refreshing of memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's simply a refreshing exercise. The witness has stated something which is very close to what is in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. There is urgency that we take our break now. We will come back at quarter to 6.00 and will continue with this objection. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, Mr. Neuner explained that he wants to use this document to refresh the memory of the witness and that the witness testifies to some things that are in this document. Do you have anything further so say, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could just have a brief look at the document which is in front of you. You find here Mr. Mahmuljin under number 2, and do you agree that Mr. Mahmuljin was appointed in October 1992 to the post of deputy chef de cabinet?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Having worked yourself as chef de cabinet, could you explain to the Chamber what the role, tasks and responsibilities of a deputy chef de cabinet is?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, while I was chef de cabinet, this is not what the establishment structure was like. There was the chef de cabinet, or head of office, and during my time there, there was Sakib Mahmuljin. Now, not in my time. This was the situation after I had left that you had a chef de cabinet and a deputy chef de cabinet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, we understand that. The question is not about the structure of the chef de cabinet. The question is: If you do know do you know what the responsibilities of the deputy chef de cabinet are, or were at the time. If you do know. If there was no deputy chef de cabinet in your time and you don't know, then you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no deputy at that time, and Sakib Mahmuljin was not a deputy. He was a secretary. That was his post, and I don't know what the duties of a deputy were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell me, because I understood your testimony to say that you were in some contact with Mr. Mahmuljin, could you tell me what -- what Mr. Mahmuljin told you what he was doing for Mr. Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Mahmuljin dealt with all the correspondence from the office of the Chief of Staff, when it came to visitors and such matters, Madam Sadika dealt with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry I'm not sure I understand. Now you say Mahmuljin dealt with all correspondence from the office of the Chief of Staff. When it came to visitors and matters, Madam Sadika that dealt with that. Now is it Madam Sadika or Mahmuljin who dealt with these things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Sadika had the duty to receive visitors, whereas Mr. Mahmuljin was the one who received correspondence and who answered requests or wrote documents back. This is something that Madam Sadika didn't know how to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that Mr. Mahmuljin was preparing documents for Mr. Halilovic to work with?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you tell me how long did Mr. Mahmuljin remain in that position, as deputy chef de cabinet of Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Neuner, the witness said he doesn't know anything about the post of deputy. Mr. Mahmuljin was --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me how long Mr. Mahmuljin remained in the position of secretary of Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Mahmuljin occupied that post until General Delic was appointed commander and when Sefer Halilovic's office was abolished. After that time, he no longer had a secretary, so this was the state of affairs until the month of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me in the early month of 1993 [sic] where was Mr. Mahmuljin located. Was he in Sarajevo or outside Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You mean January, when I say early month.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, from January to June 1993 in the time period when also he was at the service to Mr. Halilovic, as I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. You must have misunderstood what I said. I left in October 1992 and not in January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I didn't mean to say that you left in January 1993. I was asking with my last question for the whereabouts of Mr. Mahmuljin in -- let's put it the first six months of 1993. Was Mr. Mahmuljin in the first six months of 1993, located in Sarajevo or outside?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he was in Sarajevo, in the period you're referring to. That is to say, between January and June.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How many times did you meet Mr. Mahmuljin in this time-period?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Apart from responding to correspondence which Mr. Halilovic received, do you know what else Mr. Mahmuljin was doing?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Once Rasim Delic assumed the post of commander of the ARBiH, could you tell me where was Mr. Mahmuljin in the second half of 1993. Was he again in Sarajevo or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: I can tell you that he was not in Sarajevo. In the second half of 1993, Mr. Mahmuljin was in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And what was he doing in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, you also don't know what orders, if any, Mr. Delic issued in the second half of 1993 to Mr. Mahmuljin?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You haven't seen a single order, if any is existing?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to now come to the time-period when you were in the administration for logistics at the General Staff. And I understood you to say that you were there until August 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was your superior in the administration of logistics at the time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Safet Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And once Mr. Delic was appointed in June 1993 to the post of commander of the ARBiH, to whom did Mr. Safet Tihic report to?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: To Mr. Siber.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And Mr. Siber reported to whom?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: It would be only logical that he would report to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mean Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. He was the deputy of Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that until August 1993, when you remained in the logistical administration, there were at least two superiors above you, and the third such superior was then Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So, in fact, did you have any direct dealings until August 1993 with Mr. Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that you didn't attend any meetings in the days and weeks to follow Rasim Delic's appointment in June 1993, meetings at which Mr. Delic was present?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't attend any meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you also did not receive any minutes of meetings which were attended by Rasim Delic, which could tell you what was discussed at those meetings.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So I want to turn now to the -- to your move to the personnel administration. I understood you to say that sometime in August Mr. Vranj was your superior at this personnel administration. Is this right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When exactly did you move to the personnel administration?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: I think it was in the beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you tell me who Mr. Vranj report to?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: For the most part Mr. Izetbegovic, to the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is this -- I was actually asking for the formal chain of reporting. In the formal chain of command, to whom was Mr. Vranj reporting to?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: He should have reported to General Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So, in fact, once you moved to the administration for personnel, there was one superior in between you and Rasim Delic, was it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you explained a lot today to us that you, from time to time, went into the room of Rasim Delic and submitted certain documents for his signature. Were these the only occasions when you had direct dealings with Mr. Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So I'm referring to occasions where you had citations, awards with you, as you explained, and you needed a signature from Mr. Rasim Delic. These were the only meetings. Can you confirm that, please, if it's true?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You talked a lot about appointments, or proposals for appointments and possible candidates for appointments. Could you tell me within the personnel administration which subunit or subsection was responsible to prepare appointments?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: It was the first section, or the first subunit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What's the name of the first subunit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: It was the personnel department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who was in charge of the personnel department in summer 1993?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: It was Mr. Rasim Mekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you explained to us that you were in another section and that is the section for decorations, citations. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that whenever appointments were to be prepared, that only the section for personnel affairs was involved and not your unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You explained to us that you were heading or you were chief of the section for education, decoration and citations. And you explained that there was a second unit headed by Mr. Mekic. This section for personnel affairs. My question to you is: If material documentation for an appointment is being prepared, that this is exclusively in the ambit of the personnel affairs section?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: I will have to explain a bit. In this department -- Rasim Mekic worked in department, but the personnel issues were dealt with by committee because there was me, there was Rasim Mekic, and Salko Polimac; and I have tried to explain -- the whole day I've been explaining this that he was Rasim Mekic was in the period of time when people were know how to do these things. So I was there on the committee. There was Salko Polimac and there was Rasim Mekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me who set up that committee?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Sulejman Vranj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if proposals for appointments were coming in, what was the committee doing with it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Well, the proposals would be prepared and then we would sit in commission or committee to decide who will be proposed and further for the proposal forwarded to the Presidency. For the promotion into ranks because this would have to be sent to the president. This was within the ambit of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that ultimately the Presidency of RBiH decided about the acceptance of new positions, promotions and ranks?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you confirm that Rasim Delic was also member of that expanded Presidency of the RBiH during the war?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you move on, Mr. Neuner what did you want us to do with PT6289.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe that the witness has -- I would ask that the document be admitted, if it is possible. Yeah, I see the reaction, your colleague. I'm not seeking to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wouldn't have brought it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you briefly for visits outside Sarajevo. Is it correct that once during the war you went outside Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not only once, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me from June 1993 onwards, on how many occasions did you go outside Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: On four occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand what we mean by going out of Sarajevo. You mean if you just decide to go to Zenica and come back the same day or go out of Sarajevo to stay there for sometime holding your post there. What is actually the question, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain me how you could get out of Sarajevo -- I will come to -- I will try to establish the mode of travel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the mode of travel, I'm asking about the purpose when you say -- you see if you ask me how many times I have been out of The Hague, I can't remember how many times. But if you say to me how many times have I have been out The Hague to go and hold a position in Amsterdam or in Rotterdam then I may be able to remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm asking this question because Sarajevo was encircled at the time, and therefore it was not very easy to get out, and I was trying to ask the witness about his experiences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You may proceed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How could you get out of Sarajevo on these four occasions?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Through the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, since when was the tunnel operating?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Since the summer of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Any particular month you would remember in 1993 when it was opened?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what was your first occasion that you left through the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: The first time was in September, when Mr. Delic had to go and inspect the corps and to introduce himself as the new commander. So Sulejman Vranj, the General, and I went. Both of us were from the personnel department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you said in September. This is in September 1993 you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you just tell the Trial Chamber which corps were visited, if any?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. First, we went to the 6th corps because it was closest to Konjic and then to Zenica to the 3rd corps. From there we went to the 2nd Corps and then we returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me whom the delegation consisting of Mr. Delic, Vranj, and yourself who were you visiting in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: We inspected or visited the command of the 3rd Corps. We were introduced to the assistant commanders and the other personnel there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the meeting in Zenica with the corps command?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: The purpose of the meeting was to inform -- or to introduce the commander to the corps, because he had only been appointed commander two months earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who was the 3rd Corps commander to whom Mr. Delic was introduced?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: If I remember, I think it was Hadzihasanovic, Enver.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want turn now to -- just tell me how many days did you remain in this 3rd Corps AOR with Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: I think two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to turn now to awards. You have testified a lot about awards today. Could you confirm that mainly there were two laws and regulations which were applied in the procedure of awarding incentives, and this is the rules of awarding the golden lily from October 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And also the book of rules on acknowledgment and incentives of the ARBiH which is from the 31st December 1994.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So these two rules and regulations governed basically the awarding procedure. Is it right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you something about, you testified that your office, when it received proposals from the corps, did not question the facts which were submitted but, rather, assessed them only? Could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify what you mean exactly by "assess"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understood you to say and that's why I'm asking you for clarification that the corps submitted proposals which contained facts on each individual, why the person should be awarded, and I understood you to say that your office was not questioning these facts, but, rather, only assessing whether the facts would qualify that this person receives an award.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think and I may be mistaken here, I thought the witness all he checked was whether things were done according to procedure, according to the rules.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So could you describe when you would get a proposal from a corps how would your check look like. If certain facts relating to one person are stated and pleaded, what would your office do?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: With every name there was a statement of reasons what this person -- what this person did and why he is proposed for an award and if this statement of reasons was in keeping with the rules, then we would just process it, because it had come from the corps and they had sent it according to the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you tell me what would happen if the facts pleaded for an applicant would not fit into the procedure. How would your decision then look like?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Such a proposal would not get an okay from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Would the corps who submitted the proposal initially have a chance to polish up this initial proposal submit more facts or it would be denied forever?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: It wouldn't have an opportunity to polish it up because there was no time for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So what you're saying in essence is an applicant was -- or a proposal related to one person, and once it was denied it was denied forever?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: For that particular occasion, yes. Now, if another explanation or statement of reasons was submitted on the following occasion, then he could get an okay or a green light.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned background checks about the criminality of persons who were proposed for awards. And did I understand you correctly that the corps would perform such background checks?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What would happen if a corps is proposing to you a person for an award and you would have independent information available which would tell you that this person might have a criminal background? What would you do, or what have you done during the war in such a situation?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: I did not have -- I was not privy to such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. So do you mean that you never consulted with the security administration of the General Staff whether a person could have a criminal background or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No, I did not check this. Wasn't my duty to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this is PT4064. And while it is coming up, I can introduce it already. It is the rules about the awarding of golden lilies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You spoke a little bit earlier about this. Can you confirm that, in fact your office applied this regulation in the awarding procedure?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: First of all, I don't understand this date. It says the 1st of October, 1990. If that is the date for this -- for these rules, then this is it from the system of the old, the former army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I agree with you. I also noticed the date. If you look at the right-hand side at the stamp next to it, you see it is stamped on the 1st of October, 1992. And if we can maybe go for a second to the last page and look at the signature. Maybe it becomes a little bit clearer then from which time-period it is. If we could scroll to the right exactly that the signature can be seen. Maybe we can even enlarge it a little bit. Do you know whose signature that is?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sefer Halilovic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you apply rules about golden lilies as signed by Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No. I applied the rules from 1994, the 31st of October, of 31st October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But you explained to us that you came to the personnel administration already by August 1993. So what rules did you apply then to award golden lilies? The law you were referring to previously is from 1994; that's why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were rules that were made -- prepared in 1993 also.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. So you didn't apply this rule here?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm nevertheless interested in Article 9 which is now in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could enlarge or -- yeah. That a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you just look at Article 9 and if you say you cannot comment upon it, no problem, I will move on. It says here that the golden lily may be taken away from the recipient in case he or she commits a crime against humanity, the political system, life, and for reasons of self-interests, following receipt of the decoration. Is this rule familiar with you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No. At this time, I was not involved with a lily and I have no idea who conferred these. I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just that I understand that, so throughout the time from August 1993 onwards until the end of the war, a similar provision to revoke that a golden lily was awarded was never applied in your office. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether, nevertheless, there were situations that after a golden lily was awarded new facts about the criminal background of a person or whatsoever were coming to light and whether your office then withdrew golden lilies?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: We never received such a demand, nor did we have any information about such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So do I understand you correctly, that once golden lilies were awarded in your office, they were not revoked by your office later for reasons of -- that the recipient was involved in crime?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I showed a lot of patience up to a point. The witness couldn't be clearer that this -- these rules were not applicable, and that such a rule that was -- as was suggested by the Prosecutor was not applicable. So I don't see why the Prosecutor is asking this question over again, why whether this rule was applied and so on. I think we've gone too far, and I don't think the witness should answer questions like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Well, all I wanted to get at is a simple yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is you have asked this question before and it has been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm prepared to move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm not seeking that this document is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were shown a series of documents relating to the award of golden lilies and silver shields today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we can just, out of the several documents, pull one document up. For example, Exhibit 1134.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have seen this earlier. And if we can just go to the last page in the B/C/S. In English it's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we can scroll down, yeah. I want to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here, and I think you testified about this, that we see the signature from Rasim Delic, is it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Would you accept that if a commander is putting a signature below a document that he assumes authorship for it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No. I'm the author of the document, and I drafted the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would accept that you're the drafter of the document. But why are you the author? Because you haven't signed it.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: The author of the document is the person who drafts the document, if my understanding is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But you didn't sign this document, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You walked to Mr. Rasim Delic in order to get his authority over the document, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: I went to the office in order that the commander may sign document that I wrote, and that the document may be implemented. The personnel administration is responsible for the document it drafts, specifically my department as well. The commander was not duty-bound to check whether I had properly drafted the document or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is correct. But my question was that didn't you walk to Mr. Delic because you wanted to have his authority other the document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: This is a play of words now, "authority." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I put you for a moment in the position of the receiver of such a document, would you think that it would make a difference for the receiver of such a document, whether Mr. Rasim Delic had signed the document or whether you had signed the document?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Probably yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And why is that so? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Because it concerns the commander, on the one hand, and a head of a department. There's a difference in ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on. I want to move now to the second set of rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this is PT6291.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I hope you can read it. The extract is on the left column here. It refers to -- it is below the number 553. And we see here first of all the title, the book of rules on acknowledgment and incentives in the armed forces of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- ARBiH.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to my colleague Mr. Neuner but could he be so kind as to tell us once more what the purpose of showing this document to the witness is since this document was not on the 65 ter list either. I mean, the Prosecution 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. I can respond by stating that the document has been there its entirety disclosed to you, including the translation, that you yourself have the same document on your own exhibit list, and in fact, it is D978. The problem for the Prosecution was that there's only one article out of this rules and regulations translated, and we took the liberty to translate the entire law.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour this is not what I'm referring to. I agree with all was said. What I am asking is that the Prosecutor explain to us what the purpose of showing this document to the witness can be, since the document was not on the Prosecution list, and rule 85 governs the procedure and the presentation of evidence by the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, subject to correction by you or anybody else, the Chamber has a document before it which is called Prosecution's exhibit list for Witness Loncaric. And this document lists this exhibit -- this PT6291 as a 65 ter exhibit, number PT6291. I'm not sure what meaning we are supposed to give to the title 65 ter exhibit on this document. It leaves us with the impression that it was in the 65 ter list. Can we be corrected?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, according to the PT number, it seems that it was on the 65 ter list. The fact of the matter is that it was not on the 65 ter list, and that's the basis of my objection. And let me tell you briefly that the basis of my objection is that Rule 65 regulates closely how and in what way the parties lead their evidence. The Prosecution was duty-bound to present the evidence that is crucial to their case during presentation of their evidence. They can lead new evidence exceptionally according to the rules and procedure provided for that case. You know that there is the stage called rebuttal, and there are standards governing when the new evidence can be led. If new evidence is asked to be led, then it has to be evidence which the Prosecution had not had in its possession in the relevant time. This piece of evidence does not fall into either of these categories. The case law has well established the precedents. Let's look Prosecution against Zejnil Delalic, which clearly regulates the matter I've just presented and that's that the parties need to abide by the rule, by rules 85 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and that the crucial evidence, evidence crucial to the Prosecution case must be led during the Prosecution case and that exceptions will be allowed only when new evidence emerges which the Prosecution, in other words, had not had in its possession, and during rebuttal which is a completely separate stage of trial. Through the Hadzihasanovic case and through the guidelines in the Prlic case exceptions were laid down, and the exceptions include refreshing a witness's memory and the exception is based on these decisions where a document is used to impeach a witness. It is on this basis, Your Honour, that I am requesting that the Prosecutor state his intentions in showing this document. If he intends to show the document on the matter of refreshing a witness's memory or impeaching the witness then I do not object. However, if the Prosecutor wishes to use this point in time to lead new evidence that he omitted to lead at the time when they had their case to present, then I object to that, because I believe that such conduct violates the Articles 20 and 21 of the statute, since such a course encroaches upon the right of the accused to a fair trial in the element guaranteeing him enough time to prepare his Defence. I apologise. I have spoken a bit too long, but I am referring to all the documents that the Prosecution did not place on their 65 ter list. That's why I used this occasion to elaborate on my objection so that I would -- so that I can avoid doing so in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honours this is the precise issue that the Trial Chamber ruled upon on the 18th of March 2008 and which is now the subject of an interlocutory appeal in this case. The simple fact of the matter is the document which Your Honour indicates has a 65 ter number was not - and I stress - was not on the Prosecution's 65 ter exhibit list that was filed prior to trial. We have assigned it numbers so that it could be uploaded into e-court. That is the reason that these documents get numbers by the parties. So it is not an issue of we're trying to sneak some late document in and give it a 65 ter number to try to fool anyone into thinking that it was on our 65 ter list prior to trial. It was not. The Prosecution is relying upon the Trial Chamber's earlier decision. You will recall on the 18th of March this issue came up when there was a document that was not on our original 65 ter list that I showed to a witness, I believe, or one of my colleagues did, and this issue the Trial Chamber decided that we were allowed to do this. The Defence sought certification the Trial Chamber granted the certification and appeal briefs have been filed by the parties on this very point. And so partially as a result of that, on the 18th of March, when the Chamber rendered its oral decision granting certificate, I specifically asked if we were permitted to continue doing this while the appeal was pending, and if I'm not mistaken on page 7729 of the hearing on the 18th of March, from lines 13 to 21, I asked that question, and Judge Harhoff was presiding, and affirmed that the Prosecution was permitted to do this while the appeal was pending. And that's really where we are with this issue. It has been decide that the Trial Chamber allowed us to do this, the Defence appealed, sought certification and has appealed; and the Trial Chamber has stated on the 18th of March that we were allowed to do this while the appeal was pending, and I really think that we need not spend a whole lot of additional time on this point. The issue is now before the Appeals Chamber and that's where we stand on this very issue as to whether or not we can show documents to Defence witnesses that were not on our original 65 ter list that was filed months a month and months and months ago before we even knew who the Defence witnesses would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, briefly, I don't know, it is possible that it was so decided, but that was not my understanding of what Judge Harhoff said. But this does not mean that I will not raise my objection in every such situation. What will happen if our appeal is granted, and we will have all this evidence admitted? I will most definitely raise an objection against every such document because the Prosecution is aware of the fact that this largely departs from the case law of this Tribunal. I will be raising my objection in every such situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to confirm, you said you don't know whether the Trial Chamber did grant this permission. Are you able to confirm by looking at the record of the day, of the 18th of March, so that at least we can be at idem on that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies. We seem to be at logger heads here. I do -- at cross purposes. I do know that the Trial Chamber granted certification for our appeal. What I do not remember is that His Honour Judge Harhoff stated what my colleague Mr. Mundis just said, that the procedure is allowed to go ahead. I may be mistaken. Perhaps my colleague Mundis is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is precisely what I was asking you. Can you just scroll back to the transcript of 18th of March and check whether the Trial Chamber did grant permission for the further granting of these kind of documents pending the appeal. And Judge Harhoff says to me that, yes, he did grant that permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is page 7729 of the 18th of March, 2008, lines 13 through 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you find that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if my colleague Mr. Mundis found it on the transcript, I'm not challenging that. Let me just state for the record that, I will be raising my objections nevertheless because I do not want to find myself in a difficult situation. Should our appeal be grant I will ask for all that evidence to be excluded from the case file, and if I raise objections that will facilitate tracking these documents down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much Madam Vidovic. That is what I was going to suggest that given the fact that the Trial Chamber has granted the permission, and this permission is pending the appeal, the outcome of the appeal. We continue to admit the documents. If the appeal goes against the Prosecution then we strike out all that evidence. But, similarly I think I'm not quite sure whether this is the same issue and please do correct me. Yesterday we accepted a number of documents marked for identification and I thought they were more or less along the same basis. Is it so that if the appeal goes against the Defence those documents marked for identification yesterday will then also go in? Or are they on a different footing?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that was on a different footing. Not this one. Quite something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You agree with that. Thank you very much. We're learning. In that event -- that event, then we will allow this document, pending appeal.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just -- as the counsel concerned want to place an observation on the record. At this point in time I'm only showing the document to this witness. I was at this point in time not even seeking to tender the document into evidence. I just wanted to state that it could be, depending on the witness's answers, that there is even no necessity to tender this particular document into evidence. I cannot say as the counsel who has selected this document for the time being. I cannot say where I will arrive at some later point in time during the examination. I just wanted to place this observation on the record from the intervention from my learned colleague so far I was not even allowed to show the document to the witness, or to put it different, to ask a question after I have shown it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have any comment on that, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't, Your Honour. I wanted to learn from the Prosecutor whether his intention was to refresh the witness's memory or to impeach him, because in that case I would not have raised my objection and this one sentence from the Prosecutor could have solved the entire matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe again it goes to the question of timing. Maybe jump at the time when he seeks to tender it, rather than in advance. You may proceed Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, if could you just have a look at the title. That's where we stopped a moment ago. It says here: Book of rules on acknowledgments and incentives in the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The question which I wanted to put to you is: Is this the law from the December 1994 which was applied in your office to issue awards?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we could look for a moment at Article 2 and the first sentence of it. It says here and I quote: "Acknowledgment and incentives may be awarded to an individual to command, unit and institution of armed forces ..." Could you explain to Your Honours why was it foreseen by the rules that also units of the ARBiH could get acknowledgments?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: Well, pursuant to the rules, the units can get that. I don't understand your question. That's what the rules were like, and they were implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you just explain why was it not sufficient to award individuals? Why was it necessary, so to speak, to award entire units? This is my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecutor should first ascertain if the witness was a member of parliament or whether he authored the rules and could therefore talk about what the intentions of the legislator were. Otherwise, the witness is called to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I understood the witness's testimony correctly, he has applied the rule, after it was enacted as the chief of the section of awards and medals, so I believe he is in a competent position to answer that question which I just put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But your question, Mr. Neuner, had been and I'm reading at page 87, line -- starting at line 12, Could you explain to Your Honours why I'm sure it meant to be it was foreseen by the rules that also units of the ARBiH could get acknowledgments. Now, foreseen that is at the stage of parliament. That is the stage of legislations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm prepared to rephrase the question, Your Honours, sorry, I didn't see that meaning at the time I was asking. But I'm certainly prepared to rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain to Your Honours what the normal reasons were, once they were pled in an application which justified that your section in the personnel administration granted an award to a unit.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: The rules were issued and signed by the Defence minister, I believe. It had nothing to do with the General Staff or with my department. I implemented what they wrote. I did not take part in the drafting of the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, you're not answering my question. I try to make it simpler. What quality needed a unit to have in order to be eligible for an award?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA LONCARIC
utterances.text: That question should be put to the proposing party, i.e., the corps what sort of criteria they took into consideration in proposing a unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's see if we can get this a little easier. In the course of your duties in this position, did you ever receive a request from the corps for an award to a unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to remember where you sit in that request what the reasons were for the award to the unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The statement of reasons would say that the unit accomplished the missions it was given without going into great detail about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will continue from that point on, but tomorrow morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. We will then adjourn. We are adjourning to tomorrow morning at 9.00, sir. So do remember to come early in the morning. Court adjourned to tomorrow at 9.00. Same courtroom. Court adjourned.
